texts.preamble: Smt.Hanumanthamma W/O.Mareppa vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 March, 2020 Author: B.M.Shyam Prasad Bench: B.M. Shyam Prasad 1 In The High Court Of Karnataka Dharwad Bench Dated This The 20th Day Of March 2020 Before The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad W. P. No.145620 Of 2020 (Gm-Res) Between Smt.Hanumanthamma W/O .Mareppa Kudiyu Neeru Ghataka, Desanur Road, Age : 45 Years, R/O :Ward No.3, Siraguppa Siruguppa-583121, Dist :Ballari ... Petitioner (By Sri. J. M. Anilkumar, Sri. Jayawant Savagaon, Advocates) And 1. The State Of Karnataka Food Security Commissioner, Vikas Soudha, Bengaluru-560001. 2. Designated Officer Food And Safety And Standards, Ballari -583101. 3. Food And Safety Officer, Area Siraguppa Dist : Ballari-583121 ... Respondents
texts.facts: The petitioner is aggrieved by the third respondent's orders seizing the R.O. water units under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the Act'). It is undisputed that the third respondent has initiated the aforesaid proceeding for seizure because the petitioner has not obtained necessary BIS certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
texts.arguments: 2 The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a respectable resident and social service oriented citizen of Siraguppa town and has installed the R.O. water plant for the use of the villagers during summer season on a non-profitable basis and the Sub-Divisional Lab, Sindhanur, Raichur District has issued a analysis result as "potable water" on 14.01.2019, and Certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards would be required only when water is sold as packaged drinking water. If a facility is set up for the benefit of the community for disbursing water in cans, such certification would not be required. 3 A Division Bench of this Court in Lochamesh B Hugar v. Union of India and others reported in (2013) 2 KLJ 643, relying upon the provisions of Food and Safety Standards (Food Products, Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, more specifically regulation 2.10.8, has directed the Authorities to ensure that all necessary steps are taken to prohibit and prevent, manufacture and sale of packaged drinking water without certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards with further directions. The amendment reads as follows: "2.10.8 Packaged Drinking Water (other than mineral water) - 1. means water, other than natural water that is likely to be used for human consumption and that is offered or sold in packaged form, by whatever name it may be called, offered or sold" Smt.Hanumanthamma W/O.Mareppa vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30688762/ 2 This Court, in the light of the amended provisions, in a similar matter in W.P.No.45574/2018 has held as under:- 9.
